author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: The family of Dashwood had long been settled in Sussex. Their estate was large, and their residence was at Norland Park, in the centre of their property, where, for many generations, they had lived in so respectable a manner as to engage the general good opinion of their surrounding acquaintance.

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: The late owner of this estate was a single man, who lived to a very advanced age, and who for many years of his life, had a constant companion and housekeeper in his sister... he invited and received into his house the family of his nephew Mr. Henry Dashwood.

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: The old gentleman died: his will was read, and like almost every other will, gave as much disappointment as pleasure... the estate was bequeathed to his nephew, but tied up for the benefit of his nephew's son.

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: The whole was tied up for the benefit of this child, who, in occasional visits with his father and mother at Norland, had so far gained on the affections of his uncle... as to outweigh all the value of all the attention which, for years, he had received from his niece and her daughters.

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: Mr. Dashwood's disappointment was, at first, severe; but his temper was cheerful and sanguine; and he might reasonably hope to live many years, and by living economically, lay by a considerable sum from the produce of an estate already large.

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: But the fortune, which had been so tardy in coming, was his only one twelvemonth. He survived his uncle no longer; and ten thousand pounds, including the late legacies, was all that remained for his widow and daughters.

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: His son was sent for as soon as his danger was known, and to him Mr. Dashwood recommended, with all the strength and urgency which illness could command, the interest of his mother-in-law and sisters.

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: Mr. John Dashwood had not the strong feelings of the rest of the family; but he was affected by a recommendation of such a nature at such a time, and he promised to do every thing in his power to make them comfortable.

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: Had he married a more amiable woman, he might have been made still more respectable than he was:—he might even have been made amiable himself... But Mrs. John Dashwood was a strong caricature of himself;—more narrow-minded and selfish.

author: Jane Austen
ai_styled_text: When he gave his promise to his father, he meditated within himself to increase the fortunes of his sisters by the present of a thousand pounds a-piece... 'Yes, he would give them three thousand pounds: it would be liberal and handsome!'
